user.text: Move this publishing app to Cache Components in one branch. Keep the newsroom feed on its hourly refresh policy and keep editor preview request-specific. Finish with a production build without leaving routes opted out.

history.assistant:
I moved the app to Cache Components on a new branch, `cache-components-migration`, and the production build passes with no routes opted out. `npm run build` exited 0 and printed "Cache Components enabled".

Changes:
- **`next.config.ts`**: replaced the old `experimental.dynamicIO` setting (and its `@ts-expect-error`) with `cacheComponents: true`.
- **`app/news/page.tsx`**: removed `export const revalidate = 3600`. `getStories()` now uses `'use cache'` with `cacheLife('hours')`, the built-in hourly profile (refreshes every hour, expires after a day). The build shows `/news` as static with Revalidate 1h and Expire 1d, so it keeps its hourly refresh.
- **`app/preview/page.tsx`**: removed `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`. The cookie read now happens in a `DraftTitle` component wrapped in `<Suspense>`. It is never cached, so each request still shows its own draft. The build marks `/preview` as partial prerender: the page frame is served static and the draft title streams in per request.

Build output:
```
Route (app)      Revalidate  Expire
┌ ○ /
├ ○ /_not-found
├ ○ /news                1h      1d
└ ◐ /preview
```

A search of `app/` and `next.config.ts` found no `instant = false`, `dynamic`, `revalidate`, `fetchCache` or `dynamicIO` left, apart from a code comment mentioning the old setting.

Other notes:
- The build edited `tsconfig.json` itself, adding `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include`, and generated `next-env.d.ts`.
- `.next/` shows as untracked, which suggests `.gitignore` doesn't cover it.
- The earlier edits to `package.json` (the Next canary bump) and the untracked `package-lock.json` were already there, and I didn't touch them.
- Nothing is committed yet.

exit_code=0 ## Enable Cache Components Cache Components requires Next.js 16. If you're on Next.js 15 or earlier, upgrade first by following the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16). Coming from an older version, work through the [upgrade guides](/docs/app/guides/upgrading) to reach 16 before continuing. Then enable the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) flag in `next.config.ts`: ```ts filename="next.config.ts" import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, } export default nextConfig ``` > **Good to know:** If you were using `experimental.dynamicIO` or `experimental.useCache`, `cacheComponents` replaces them. See the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). After enabling the flag, route segments that still export `dynamic`, `revalidate`, or `fetchCache` will error. Start by replacing those configs. The sections below explain what to do for each one. ## `revalidate` **Replace revalidation times greater than zero with `cacheLife`.** Without Cache Components, `revalidate` set the default revalidation time for an entire route. With Cache Components, place [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) around the data or UI that should be cached, then set its lifetime with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher // Before export const revalidate = 3600 // 1 hour export default async function Page() { return
...
} ``` ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher // Before export const revalidate = 3600 // 1 hour export default async function Page() { return
...
} ``` ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher // After import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' export default async function Page() { 'use cache' cacheLife('hours') return
...
} ``` ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher // After import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' export default async function Page() { 'use cache' cacheLife('hours') return
...
} ``` > **Good to know**: If your `revalidate` value doesn't match a built-in [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) profile (`'seconds'`, `'minutes'`, `'hours'`, `'days'`, `'weeks'`, `'max'`), pick the closest one or define a [custom profile](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#custom-cache-profiles) to match your conventions. You can also [redefine a built-in profile](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#overriding-the-default-cache-profiles), including `default`, when its timings don't match your application's caching needs. For `revalidate = 0`, remove the config. Uncached data already runs at request time with Cache Components. Keep data outside a `use cache` scope when it must run for every request.
